title: Open-source Gemini Tasks alternative (formerly Spark) · {name}
description: {name} does the work on your files with the AI you choose, Gemini included, on your devices. Free, open source, and it works where Tasks in Gemini isn’t offered.
h1: An open-source alternative to Gemini Tasks, on your devices, with the AI you choose
acts: An open-source alternative to Gemini Tasks, on your devices,
lede: Tasks in Gemini, which Google first called Spark, takes on your busywork in Google’s cloud, with Google’s AI, across your Gmail, Calendar and Drive. {name} does the work in your browser tab, on the files you give it, with the AI you choose: Gemini, another company’s, or the one on your own computer. Free, open source, nothing to install, and it works where Tasks isn’t offered: in the UK, Switzerland and the European Economic Area, or on a work or school account.
fair.title: Gemini Tasks, fairly
fair.body: Tasks in Gemini is the mode Google added to the Gemini app for work you hand off: flip the toggle from Chat to Task, say what you want done, and it works in the background, then tells you when the result is ready. Google tested it as Gemini Spark from May 2026, renamed it, and on 17 November 2026 began offering it free of charge in six countries. It acts across Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs and more than 50 other apps you connect, browses the web for you, runs code on a remote computer, and hands back files: PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, presentations. It runs tasks on a schedule, asks before it sends, deletes or buys, and reads skills written as SKILL.md, as {name} does. Google calls its ability to handle tasks experimental, and asks you to supervise it.
table.rows: Wherever a browser opens it. No {name} account; a child gets a profile a parent sets.

Free of charge in Australia, Canada, India, Japan, South Korea and the US. Elsewhere with a Google AI Pro or Ultra plan, except in the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland and the UK, where it isn’t offered. For adults, on a personal Google account with History on; not on a work or school account, for now.
In your browser tab, on any recent computer, phone included. Nothing to install.
In Google’s cloud, not on your phone or computer. It browses in a remote browser, or in your own Chrome on a computer, and runs code on a remote computer.
The files you give it, inside the browser’s fence. A real folder on your computer in Chrome and Edge.
The apps you connect, Gmail, Calendar and Drive among them, the files you upload, and the websites you’re signed in to. On a Mac, its app also changes files in the folders you add.
Any, Gemini included: on this computer, a free one, your key, your plan.
Google’s own: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, or another Gemini from its menu.
The AI you choose. With the AI on this computer, nobody.

Google. Human reviewers read some chats, which are then kept up to three years. A setting lets Google train its AI on your chats, tasks and data from the apps you connect. The remote browser keeps the cookies that sign you in to websites.
With your permission, it signs in with Google or with a password saved in Google Password Manager, and pays through Google Pay, within a spending cap you set.
With the tab or the app closed
{name} works while its tab is open. A task due while it was closed runs when you’re back.

It keeps working in Google’s cloud with your devices off, and schedules start by themselves: up to 10, once a day at most, without a paid plan or with Google AI Plus; up to 50 with Pro or Ultra, as often as every hour or when an email arrives.
{name} is free; the AI may not be. A Google AI Pro or Ultra plan works too.
Free of charge in six countries, within usage limits that rise with a plan: Google AI Plus at $4.99 a month, Pro at $19.99, Ultra from $99.99. Elsewhere it takes Pro or Ultra.
Yes, MIT. Anyone can read every line.
Google’s pages offer no source code.
A folder IT serves from its own address, behind its gateway and sign-in.
Not for now: it takes a personal Google account, not a work or school one.
Plain files and backups. Gemini’s export comes in.
Google exports your Gemini history on request, and a skill downloads as a .zip. Deleting your history doesn’t delete what the remote browser and computer keep, which has a setting of its own.
better.title: Where Gemini Tasks does better
better.items: It keeps working in Google’s cloud with your phone and computer off, and starts a task on a schedule or when an email arrives. {name} works while it is open.

It acts inside the Google apps you already use: it sorts and answers email in Gmail, manages Calendar, changes Docs and Sheets, and reaches more than 50 other apps, OpenTable and Instacart among them.
It browses for you, fills in forms and can pay, asking first. {name} reads the pages you allow, and never touches passwords or payments.
You can hand it work without opening it, in the US to start: forward an email to its address, or text it. It has phone apps and a Mac app.
In six countries it is free of charge, AI included, with nothing to choose. {name} asks you to choose an AI first.
both.title: Use both
both.cards: Google AI Pro or Ultra, on a computer, through This computer: a line you paste once, with Antigravity CLI installed and signed in. No second subscription.
In Google Takeout, choose Gemini, and My Activity with only Gemini Apps, in JSON. Drop the file in {name}: every conversation comes in, nothing twice.
Both read SKILL.md. Those that need no program outside the browser work in {name} as they are.
catch.items: {name} works while it is open. Close the tab and it waits for you; nothing goes on in a cloud.
{name} doesn’t click through websites for you: it reads the pages you allow, and passwords and payments are never its to touch.
{name} is free; the AI behind it may not be.
Your Gemini plan needs This computer: a line to paste once, on a computer, with Antigravity CLI installed and signed in.
The AI on this computer needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip. Not on phones.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
faq.items: Is there an open-source alternative to Gemini Tasks?
{name} is free and MIT. It does the work on your files with any AI, Gemini included, and the AI on this computer costs nothing.
Google renamed it. It tested Spark with its subscribers from May 2026, then called it Task, a mode beside Chat in the Gemini app; its pages now say Tasks in Gemini.
Is Gemini Tasks available in the UK or Europe?
Not for now. Google’s help says it isn’t offered in the European Economic Area, Switzerland or the United Kingdom, whatever the plan. {name} works there, as it does anywhere.
In six countries: Australia, Canada, India, Japan, South Korea and the US, within usage limits. Elsewhere it takes a Google AI Pro or Ultra plan, where Google offers it.
Yes, Google AI Pro or Ultra, on a computer, through This computer: you paste a line once, with Antigravity CLI installed and signed in. A key from Google works too, on any device.
Does Google read what I hand to Tasks?

Its privacy hub says human reviewers read some chats, kept up to three years, and that a setting lets Google train its AI on your chats, tasks and data from connected apps. With {name} and the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it.
Can I use it with a work account?
Tasks in Gemini takes a personal Google account, for now. {name} asks for no account, and a company can serve it from its own address: see {enterprise}.
Is Gemini Tasks the same as NotebookLM?
No. Gemini Notebook, which was NotebookLM, answers from the sources you give it; Tasks acts across your apps. See {compare-notebooklm}.
end.title: Give {name} a file, and choose the AI that does the work
